content.overview: BNS s. 230 — Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence. BNS restatement of IPC 194. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 194. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 230 is the rule on “Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence”. The section provides that (1) Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence, intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, any person to be convicted of an offence which is capital by the law for the time being in force in India shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 230 exists so that “Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence” has a closed legal test in Chapter XIV — Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Perjury, screening, harbouring, false charge, and failing to appear on a bond.

The provision in detail
230. (1) Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence, intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, any person to be convicted of an offence which is capital by the law for the time being in force in India shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees

(2) If an innocent person be convicted and executed in consequence of false evidence referred to in sub-section (1), the person who gives such false evidence shall be punished either with death or the punishment specified in sub-section (1)

Essential ingredients
1. (1) Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence, intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, any person to be convicted of an offence which is capital by the law for the time being in force in India shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees
2. (2) If an innocent person be convicted and executed in consequence of false evidence referred to in sub-section
3. (1), the person who gives such false evidence shall be punished either with death or the punishment specified in sub-section

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 230 (Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 230 (Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence), Chapter XIV — Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) (1) Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence, intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, any person to be convicted of an offence which is capital by the law for the time being in force in India shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees
   (2) (2) If an innocent person be convicted and executed in consequence of false evidence referred to in sub-section
   (3) (1), the person who gives such false evidence shall be punished either with death or the punishment specified in sub-section
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 230 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 230 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
